title: Password recovery turns the entrance into a member directory: submit the same address twice and a registered one errors while an unregistered one succeeds
evidence: out/entry/06-forms.json + out/entry/02-disclosure.json. AS THE VISITOR SEES IT (screenshots out/entry/06-forgot-*.png): owner@gamos.demo submit #1 -> 3519 ms, neutral success 'אם הכתובת רשומה במערכת, נשלח אליה קישור לאיפוס הסיסמה'; submit #2 immediately after -> 1305 ms, RED ERROR 'הפעולה נכשלה. אם הבעיה חוזרת — פנה לתמיכה.' (screenshot 06-forgot-registered-2-immediately-after.png). qa-entry-no-such-person-9143@gamos.demo submit #1 -> 1269 ms neutral success; submit #2 immediately after -> 1273 ms NEUTRAL SUCCESS AGAIN. AT THE WIRE (POST /auth/v1/recover, 3 samples each): registered = [200 in 2386 ms, 429 over_email_send_rate_limit in 350 ms, 429 in 310 ms]; unregistered = [200 in 311 ms, 200 in 304 ms, 200 in 297 ms]. Two independent separators: (a) status — a 429 on the second request means the address exists, a 200 means it does not, deterministic, no statistics needed; (b) time — the first request is 2386 ms for a registered address against 297-311 ms for an unregistered one, a 7x gap.
repro: Open https://app.inplace.digital/forgot-password. Type any address, press 'שליחת קישור איפוס'. Press browser Back, type the SAME address, press again. A registered address shows the red failure banner; an unregistered address shows the same neutral success both times. Or POST twice to /auth/v1/recover with the anon key and read the second status.
expected: The answer must be indistinguishable for a registered and an unregistered address in message text, HTTP status, body shape AND response time — the rule ForgotPassword.tsx:12-20 states about itself ('a login screen must not double as a member directory').
actual: The rate limiter only fires when there is a mailbox to send to, so its 429 — and the 2.1 s the send costs — announce that the address is registered. The screen's own neutral sentence is correct; the failure branch behind it is not.

title: On a phone /pricing shows four plan names and four document counts and nothing else — all 52 entitlement rows are display:none with no control to open them
evidence: out/entry/05-pricing.json and out/entry/08-mobile-contrast.json. Desktop 1440x900: body innerText 2676 chars, 4 cards x 13 entitlement rows measured individually (out/entry/05-pricing-full.png). Mobile 390x844, same URL, same session: body innerText 714 chars, 0 entitlement rows, no expander, no 'more' control (screenshots out/entry/05-pricing-mobile.png and out/entry/08-mobile-pricing.png). Cause is a contradiction between two files that shipped together: src/styles/plan-card.css:1049 has '@media (max-width: 767px) { .plan-block { display: none; } }' and :1053 '.plan-card__more { display: block; }', while src/components/PlanTicket.tsx:51-54 states it deliberately does NOT draw .plan-card__more because 'this card already lists every row it received inline, at every width, so the expander would hide what is already there'. The stylesheet hides the rows and hands them to an expander the component chose not to render.
repro: Open https://app.inplace.digital/pricing at 390x844 (or on any phone). Scroll the whole page. No plan lists a single capability.
expected: A visitor on a phone can tell the plans apart. The rows are the page's entire job — /pricing is the only public page that says what the product does.
actual: Free/Basic/Pro/Premium are distinguishable only by a document count. The rows remain in the DOM (a screen reader still gets them), so this is invisible to any check that reads markup rather than layout. The same PlanTicket is used by /settings/subscription, which is likely affected the same way — that route belongs to another agent.

title: Sign-in leaks whether an address is registered through a constant ~85 ms timing gap whose ranges never overlap
evidence: out/entry/02-disclosure.json + out/entry/03-timing-lockout.json. POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with an invented password. Run A (registered first in each pair, owner@gamos.demo): registered 343/410/318->395/400 ms => [395,400,410,595]; unregistered [309,309,318,343]. Run B (unregistered FIRST in each round, accountant@gamos.demo, plus a SHORT unknown address to rule out address length): registered [481(cold),419,402,399,396]; unknown-short zzq9x@gamos.demo [820(cold),323,320,317,328]; unknown-long [336,311,324,312,314]. Median registered 402 ms vs 316 ms unknown. Excluding the first cold request of each run, the two ranges do not overlap at all (registered min 396 > unknown max 343), so a single threshold at ~370 ms separates 9/9 samples. Address length is not the cause: the SHORTER unknown address (321 ms median) is as fast as the longer one (313 ms). Status (400) and body ({"code":400,"error_code":"invalid_credentials","msg":"Invalid login credentials"}) are byte-identical in every sample, and the on-screen message is correctly generic — 'אימייל או סיסמה שגויים.' (screenshot out/entry/03-login-failed-message.png).
repro: POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password twice with the same invented password, once with owner@gamos.demo and once with a fake local part at the same domain. Time each. Repeat 4 times, interleaved.
expected: Indistinguishable in message, status, body shape and response time.
actual: Message, status and body are correct; the clock is not. This deploy makes it worse rather than better: 0296/0303/0310 add a Postgres advisory lock plus an upsert to the password-verification path, and that work runs ONLY when a user row exists — so the counter built to slow an attacker down also widens the oracle that tells the attacker which addresses are worth attacking. Combine with ENTRY-04 (no throttle at all on addresses that do not exist) and the tenant list is enumerable at full speed.

title: No sign-in throttle of any kind was observable, and the switch that turns the new lockout on is a manual owner step the rollout notes record as blocked
evidence: out/entry/03-timing-lockout.json, 'burst'. 12 consecutive wrong-password POSTs to /auth/v1/token for qa-entry-lockout-probe-7761@gamos.demo, 400 ms apart: 12 x HTTP 400, 301/308/311/312/312/313/314/318/319/325/327 ms, no 429, no growing delay, no captcha, no change in the body. The lockout in 0310 keys on event->>'user_id' and returns 'continue' when it is null, so it can never fire for an address with no user row — the anonymous surface is unthrottled by construction. Whether it fires for a REAL account is NOT measured: docs/ROLLOUT-0291-0313-NOTES.md §4 says the enabling switch is 'node scripts/auth-hardening.mjs --with-lockout', owner-only, and that 'ה-PATCH לייצור נחסם על ידי מסווג ההרשאות של סביבת הסוכן'; supabase/config.toml declares no [auth.hook.password_verification_attempt] section, so nothing in the repository proves GoTrue was ever pointed at the function 0296 created.
repro: POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password twelve times with a fake address and any password. Every answer is an identical 400 in ~310 ms.
expected: Either a throttle the caller can feel, or an explicit statement that unknown addresses are deliberately not throttled. Ruling #347 promises ten failures in a rolling fifteen minutes locks an account.
actual: Unlimited attempts against addresses that do not exist, at full speed. I stopped at 4 wrong-password attempts on owner@gamos.demo and 5 on accountant@gamos.demo — reaching the threshold of 10 would have locked a demo account the other agents in this sweep are signing in with, so THE LOCKOUT ITSELF IS UNVERIFIED IN PRODUCTION. Someone with a spare registered address should finish this measurement; it is the one gate of this deploy that a green CI run cannot speak for, because it is configuration and not code.

title: The banner says every capability is open on every plan and only volume differs; the cards directly beneath it exclude eight capabilities from Basic and eleven from Free
evidence: out/entry/05-pricing.json 'fullText' and out/entry/05-pricing-full.png. Banner (he.ts:5919, key pricingTail.notice): 'כל היכולות פתוחות בכל המסלולים; ההבדל הוא נפח בלבד.' Card 'בסיס', measured rows: 'לא כלול' on ייצוא Excel ודוחות לרו״ח, לוח ביצועי ספקים, עד 10 סניפים, התאמות בנק, תור תשלומים לרואה החשבון, חשבוניות מרכזות, חיבור למערכות אחרות, תמיכה מורחבת — eight, and one of the two blocks is titled 'אין גישה לכספים וחיבורים' (no access to money and connections). Card 'חינם': the same eight plus five capabilities marked 'כלול ב־30 הימים הראשונים בלבד'.
repro: Open https://app.inplace.digital/pricing on a desktop viewport and read the blue banner, then read the two lower cards.
expected: A public page states one thing about what a plan buys.
actual: Two answers on one screen. A visitor reading only the banner (which is all a phone visitor gets — see ENTRY-02) believes Basic includes bank reconciliation and accountant exports. It does not.

title: The Free rung breaks its own card: the trial badge leaves the card by 19 px, the label wraps one word per line, and the row is 138 px where every other plan's is 17 px
evidence: out/entry/07-badgebox.json, measured at 1440x900: card 'חינם' box left=1063 right=1273 width=209; the badge 'רק 30 יום ראשונים' box left=1044 — nineteen pixels OUTSIDE the card — width 110, white-space:nowrap, overflow:visible; badgeEscapesCard=true. The row containing it is 138 px tall. Row heights in the Free card: 17,17,138,86,121,86,104,17,17,35,17,17,17. The same rows in בסיס/פרו/פרימיום: 17 or 35. Total block height per card (out/entry/06-forms.json 'cardHeights'): חינם 893 px, בסיס 496, פרו 515, פרימיום 498, with all four cards stretched to a common 1117 px. Screenshots out/entry/07-free-rung.png (read: badge crossing the card border, 'קריאה / אוטומטית / של / מסמכים / — / פתוח / ב־30 / הימים / הראשונים' one word per line) and out/entry/05-pricing-full.png.
repro: Open /pricing at 1440x900 and look at the rightmost (Free) card.
expected: A 110 px nowrap badge and a full sentence do not share a 209 px column; a badge does not cross its card's border.
actual: The badge starves the label to about 50 px. Because the Free card's content is 1.8x its neighbours', the grid stretches all four to match, leaving 220-620 px of empty coloured fill under Premium and Pro — the 'decorative empty areas' the project constitution names as forbidden.

title: The recovery rate-limit sentence is dead code: the user is told 'the operation failed, contact support' when the truth is 'wait fifty-five seconds'
evidence: Measured: out/entry/06-forms.json 'forgot[1]' — the visible banner is 'הפעולה נכשלה. אם הבעיה חוזרת — פנה לתמיכה.' (screenshot out/entry/06-forgot-registered-2-immediately-after.png), while the wire (out/entry/02-disclosure.json) carries {"code":"429","error_code":"over_email_send_rate_limit","msg":"For security purposes, you can only request this after 55 seconds."}. Cause: src/pages/ForgotPassword.tsx:38 selects the dedicated string with /rate limit|too many/i, and GoTrue's message contains neither phrase, so t('forgotPassword.rateLimited') can never be reached and errorText's generic sentence is shown instead.
repro: Submit /forgot-password twice within a minute with any registered address.
expected: The file's own comment: 'the rate-limit failure is the one worth naming in the user's language'.
actual: A person who mistyped once and resubmitted is told the system is broken and to contact support. NOTE: the correct fix is not to name the wait — that would sharpen ENTRY-01 into a one-click oracle. The two have to be fixed together: the same answer for both address classes, then a truthful sentence.

title: Hebrew plural agreement is wrong five times on the public pricing page: '1 משתמשים פעילים', '1 סניפים'
evidence: out/entry/05-pricing.json 'pluralBreaks': ['1 משתמשים','1 סניפים','1 משתמשים','1 סניפים','1 סניפים'] — Free and Basic each render '1 משתמשים פעילים' (should be 'משתמש פעיל אחד' / '1 משתמש פעיל'), and Free, Basic and Pro each render '1 סניפים' (should be 'סניף אחד' / '1 סניף'). Visible in out/entry/05-pricing-full.png and out/entry/07-free-rung.png.
repro: Open /pricing on a desktop viewport; read the first two rows of the Free, Basic and Pro cards.
expected: Hebrew agrees in number. The repo has a guard for exactly this (check:plurals).
actual: Plural noun after the numeral 1. CLAUDE.md records check:plurals as one of the 13 verify guards that no workflow runs, which is why a green CI did not catch it.

title: GoTrue's own signup endpoint is open, so a stranger can register any address and permanently block it from ever opening a business — and the victim is told a confirmation mail was sent
evidence: Measured: GET /auth/v1/settings returns {"disable_signup":false,"mailer_autoconfirm":false,...} (out/entry/04-tokens.json 'authSettings'). It has to stay open — src/pages/AcceptInvite.tsx:105 and src/pages/AcceptOperatorInvite.tsx:84 both call supabase.auth.signUp. Consequence, read from the code and NOT executed: supabase/functions/public-signup/index.ts:447 answers the email_taken case with 202 and NEUTRAL_ANSWER ('a confirmation mail was sent'), so an address a stranger pre-registered can never be turned into an organization and its real owner sees a success message every time. src/pages/SetPassword.tsx:18-27 states the pre-hijack attack was closed by taking the password out of signup; that holds for the public-signup path only, not for /auth/v1/signup, which any visitor can call with the public anon key.
repro: NOT REPRODUCED LIVE, deliberately: proving it means creating an auth user in production. The two halves that ARE measured are the open setting above and the neutral answer in public-signup's source.
expected: An address a stranger typed into a public endpoint cannot deny its real owner the ability to sign up, and if it can, the real owner is told why rather than told a mail is on its way.
actual: Denial of registration, silent by construction, on top of the account-pre-registration that ruling #332 was written to close. Worth an owner decision (rate-limit and/or garbage-collect unconfirmed GoTrue signups that have no organization) rather than a code fix in isolation.

title: A nonexistent route is a silent bounce to /login with HTTP 200, not a 404
evidence: out/entry/01-routes.json: GET /no-such-screen -> HTTP 200, document served, client lands on /login with the sign-in card and h1 'כניסה לחשבון', body identical to /login (431 chars, screenshot out/entry/01-no-such-screen.png). src/App.tsx:392 routes '*' to Navigate to='/', and logged out '/' is the guard's Navigate to='/login'.
expected: ROUTES.md: 'a proper 404, not a silent bounce'.
actual: A silent bounce. Flagged as KNOWN because the route is on round 1's agent-6 checklist and the code path predates this deploy; I did not have the previous findings list, so I cannot say whether its severity changed. Reported only because it is on my own checklist.

title: The operator invitation refuses a bad link by naming a state; its tenant twin names a next step
evidence: out/entry/04-tokens.json. /operator-invite?token=<garbage> and /operator-invite?token= both render exactly 'הצטרפות לצוות ניהול הפלטפורמה, לא ניהול עסק הקישור אינו תקין. למסך הכניסה' (screenshots 04-operator-invite-garbage.png, 04-operator-invite-empty.png). The tenant screen at the same probe renders 'קישור ההזמנה אינו תקין. ייתכן שהועתק חלקית — בקש מהעסק לשלוח הזמנה חדשה.'
expected: The brief's own rule: a message that says what happened AND what to do next. The tenant screen meets it.
actual: 'The link is not valid' and a link back to sign-in, which is a door the holder of an operator invitation cannot walk through — they have no account yet. It should say to ask for a fresh invitation.

title: Text controls on the public entrance are 16-20 px tall on a phone, against the 44 px the product's own stylesheet says it holds to
evidence: out/entry/08-mobile-contrast.json at 390x844: /login 'שכחתי סיסמה' 20 px, 'להרשמה' 20 px, 'תנאי שימוש' 16 px, 'מדיניות פרטיות' 16 px; /signup 'התחברות' 20 px; /forgot-password 'חזרה למסך הכניסה' 19 px. Screenshots out/entry/08-mobile-*.png. src/styles/plan-card.css:1069 and Entrance.tsx:431 both cite 44 px / min-h-11 as the product's floor.
repro: Open /login at 390x844 and measure the two links under the password field and the two in the footer.
expected: The product's own 44 px floor, or a deliberate exemption for inline text links.
actual: 16-20 px. WCAG 2.1 AA carries no target-size criterion, so this is measured against the product's own standard, not against the stated AA target — which is why it is low and not medium.
